heroHeadline: Day 88 of Op Ghazab — ISPR: 11 Militants Killed in Two Datta Khel IBOs; 19-Day Cross-Border Strike Pause; Journalists Day 15–18 in Taliban Detention
heroSubtitle: On May 24, 2026 (Day 88 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), Pakistan's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) announced that security forces killed 11 Fitna al-Khawarij (TTP) militants in two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in the Datta Khel area of North Waziristan district, KPK, after 'intense and fierce exchanges of fire.' The Datta Khel operations extend the pattern of precision ground targeting inside Pakistan that has replaced cross-border aerial bombardment: no confirmed Pakistani airstrikes have struck Afghan territory since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike — a 19-day pause. The IBO campaign through May has killed: 22+ militants in Shewa sanitization (May 17-20), Afghan commander Basir in Arjam Kali (May 20), 4 including wanted commander Tor Saqib in Spinwam (May 21), and 11 in Datta Khel (May 24). Three journalists remain in Taliban detention: Paigard News Agency head Jawid Niazi (Day 18 — detained May 6), TOLO News presenter Mansoor Niazi (Day 17 — detained May 7), and TOLO News political editor Imran Danish (Day 15 — detained May 9). No formal ceasefire has been established; no Urumqi Round 2 date has been announced; China has been silent on mediation since April 8. On the humanitarian front, UNAMA's May 22 formal 'grave concern' over Taliban Decree No. 18 — which treats a girl's silence as consent to marriage — remains unanswered by the Taliban, which has rejected the characterization as Western interference in Islamic jurisprudence.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA, Express Tribune, Pakistan Today, ISPR
